::: {#rem-structural-induction}
#### Why structural induction works

Every element of a recursively defined set (@def-recursive-set) comes from the base case
by applying the recursive rule some number $k \ge 0$ of times.
Let $Q(k)$ be the claim that every element built with $k$ applications of the rule has the property $P$.
Strong induction (@def-strong-induction) on $k$ proves $Q(k)$ for every $k \ge 0$:

- an element built with 0 applications is named by the base case, so it has $P$ by the base case of @def-structural-induction;
- an element built with $k \ge 1$ applications comes, by its last application, from elements built with fewer applications,
  which have $P$ by the strong induction hypothesis, so it has $P$ by the inductive step.

So every element of the set has $P$.

:::
